models.limits: Finite response admission and view invalidation abstraction only. Context changes invalidate the request epoch; no extra implementation context comparison is assumed. Does not prove parsers, exact byte slicing, frame filtering, base64/UTF-8 decoding, React scheduling, authentication/IAM evaluation, WASI containment, Go/JS refinement, CloudWatch delivery or AWS equivalence. Actual native/runtime/console tests remain required. Shared app.js scope is limited to the compiled Lambda invocation/reveal view; other services retain their existing model scopes. server.go scope covers only Tail capability metadata, not native authorization correctness.

changes.reason: Existing scoped console behavior retained alongside read-only discovery; bounded model properties are not a proof of generated JavaScript, browser rendering, SQL or full authorization implementation.

models.limits: One Access authority; opaque disjoint fresh tokens abstract hash storage/randomness. Clock0..3/browserTTL2/participantTTL1 and login cutoff bound exploration, not API limits. No Go/cryptographic/locking/HTTP-Origin/TLS/cookie/UI/accessibility/cross-team refinement or liveness proof. UI and named tests are caller/correspondence seams, not code executed or proven by TLC; actual native/browser assertions independently check them.

Finite view acceptance/custody abstraction only, not React/AbortController/DOM/thread execution, token authentication, IAM, native receipt validity/freshness, Go/SQL, cryptography or AWS visual parity. Native requests may finish after cancellation; only current replies enter the view. Accepted history captures its original mounted/context/epoch, so later changes cannot relabel an old acceptance. Unmount epoch advance is redundant with the alive guard and the combined mutant deliberately removes both. Receipt values abstract one response identity per context/epoch; native freshness and release require actual browser/SDK tests. main.jsx source scope is only added SQS keyed-remount/navigation seam, not all other services or authentication.

Finite async-display acceptance model, not React/AbortController/DOM execution or implementation refinement. Context abstracts a group/stream/page query; parent region/principal changes unmount the component. IAM, team authentication, page tokens, SQL state and mutation atomicity are separate backend obligations. Form input, busy indicators and navigation layout are not modeled; actual stale-reply and browser tests remain required. Shared main.jsx scope covers the added Logs identity/region/navigation remount only, not all other service views or browser authentication.

Finite explicit-retrieve/display model, not React, DOM, AbortController, memory zeroization or implementation refinement. Only the successful response path is modeled; native store/IAM must authorize before returning any secret. A returned ARN can differ and must be rejected. Retrieve, Hide and navigation invalidate epochs; unmount also clears visible state. Parent must remount on region/principal changes. Emission history captures the context at each acceptance so later Hide/navigation cannot relabel an earlier stale acceptance. Draft entry, mutation atomicity and form layout are outside this model. Parent main.jsx scope binds only Secrets routing/remount key (region/principal/navigation); the generated app.js binding is the canonical compiled artifact of those source inputs, independently checked by bundle/asset hashes. It does not model unrelated existing console services or prove JavaScript compilation.

Nativepayloadbytes/schema/confirmation/keyentropy/quota/APIwire/SDK andauthenticatedcloudvisualparity areoutside. The generated app.js scope binds only the canonical compiled artifact of this separately declared Sakura child/mount projection; it does not prove bundler/compiler correctness or unrelated AWS/GCP/Azure behavior.

UI finite safety abstraction only, not JS/React/AbortController scheduling refinement, native protocol/JSON/IAM/auth/SQLite state/number/binary/size/capacity proof. TableId checks establish agreement at item-read acceptance only, not freshness after later native changes or atomic TableId-CAS on mutation; official TableName writes remain subject to recreation between preflight and send. Combined context labels abstract principal/region/remount, not credentials/tenant isolation. Stutter observation admits no liveness/hung-read progress claim. One write intent only; symbolic ACK/no automatic replay, not server rollback when an aborted request already committed. No concrete item values, missing-item/delete-confirmation semantics or arbitrary pagination. Main caller scope is limited to the DynamoDB route and its region|principal|navigation mount key/reset; embedded app.js is the canonical derived component/caller artifact. Neither binding proves other shell/components, compiler/bundler correctness or JavaScript refinement.

Finite UI protocol abstraction, not JS/React/Cloudscape/HTTP/SQL/IAM/crypto refinement or liveness. Initial key-list/Describe lookup completion is abstracted because actual source disables selection until it finishes; later target reads may overlap. Target/list revisions normalized after these reads. Excludes all parser/format/pagination/permission semantics, arbitrary key sets, repeated forms beyond bound, network ambiguity without ACK and full AWS console parity. Current list outcome and target metadata are stored fields, not derived tautologies. Retired-list mutation jointly bypasses redundant captured-object/active/abort checks; submit-target mutation abstracts both button and handler defenses. Retry mutant creates actual second pending write plus request counter, not a ghost-only edit. Root parent context key/principal binding is assumed; locale frame is only this model state, not the locale provider. Parent kms.jsx/main.jsx declarations bind only the Aliases mount and supplied region/principal/key identity; other KMS/general services remain outside. app.js is the canonical compiled correspondence artifact of that component/mount, independently checked by bundle hashes, not a proof of compilation or unrelated UI.
View acceptance and write sequencing only: native request results, DOM rendering, keyboard focus, accessibility, form conversion and React scheduling are covered by browser tests, not this model.

Finite client lifecycle contract, not JS/React/browser/fetch/WebSocket refinement. Single abstract remote lifecycle does not represent arbitrary concurrent sessions. Assumes authentic native response and component/channel identity checks; parsing, transport, DOM, token cryptography and guest termination are independent. Operation epoch is defense in depth under busy/permanent-disposal guards; no impossible overlapping operation is invented to produce an epoch-only counterexample.
